concept.name: Final settlement price
concept.definition: The price at which a cash-settled futures (or option) contract is settled at maturity, determined pursuant to a procedure specified by the exchange.
concept.intuition: The final settlement price is the official last mark of a contract's life — the single number that decides the terminal cash flows for everyone still holding it.
concept.mechanics: The exchange's contract rules define exactly how it is computed: common procedures include a special opening quotation based on constituent opening prices (equity index futures) or a volume-weighted average over a defined window. The clearing organization settles all remaining open positions against this price, and it need not equal the last traded price of the contract.
concept.failure_modes: Because the final settlement price follows its own procedure, it can deviate sharply from the contract's last traded price (e.g., an opening-rotation quotation after an overnight event), producing unexpected P&L for positions marked against the close.
concept.misconceptions: It is not simply the closing price of the futures contract on the last trading day; each product's rulebook defines a distinct calculation, and the two can differ materially.
concept.example: Quarterly S&P 500 index options settle against the special opening quotation (SOQ) of the index on expiration morning, so a trader holding through expiry is exposed to opening prices of the 500 constituents, not the prior close.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary: A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry
